blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a popular alternative for evaluation. Often referred to as LLMs as judges (LLJs), these systems have been widely adopted by researchers and practitioners across a broad range of measurement tasks, driven by their strong performance, scalability, and cost-effectiveness relative to human judgment. However, a growing body of work has shown that the use of LLJs raise concerns about their validity and reliability as evaluators. Existing efforts to address these challenges have largely focused on developing bias-mitigation techniques and refining prompting strategies. While these approaches represent an important step forward, they primarily offer technical fixes and leave a more fundamental challenge unaddressed: the lack of standardized, transparent, and reproducible evaluation practices.
In this paper, we introduce LLJ Cards , a framework that synthesizes best practices from measurement theory, natural language generation, and machine learning literature into practical guidelines for LLJ-based evaluations. While LLJs offer a promising path toward scalable evaluation, their effective use requires grounding in rigorous evaluation principles to ensure validity, reliability, and reproducibility. LLJ Cards addresses this need by providing a structured framework for applying these principles in the design and reporting of automated evaluations.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
In recent years, large language models (LLMs) as judges (LLJs) have gained significant popularity among machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) researchers and practitioners [ 33 , 56 ] . Their use has also expanded well beyond computer science, reaching into the social sciences [ 85 , 37 ] . This uptake is largely driven by their strong alignment with human judgments, which have traditionally served as the gold standard in measurement, as well as their perceived effectiveness as evaluators [ 60 , 7 ] . In addition, their flexibility, scalability, and cost efficiency have contributed to their adoption and integration into standard evaluation practices [ 15 ] .
Despite this widespread enthusiasm, a body of work has cautioned that such adoption may be premature, as numerous issues related to the validity and reliability of LLJs have been documented [ 111 , 91 , 92 , 42 , 27 , 57 , 9 , 34 ] .
blocks.zh:
近年来,大型语言模型(LLMs)作为评委(LLJs)在机器学习(ML)和自然语言处理(NLP)研究者和从业者中获得了显著的欢迎[33,56]. 它们的使用也远远超出了计算机科学,深入到了社会科学[85,37]. 之所以采用这一标准,主要是因为它们与人类的判断高度一致,而人类判断传统上是衡量的金本位标准,以及它们作为评价者被认为有效[60、7]。 此外,它们的灵活性、可扩展性和成本效益有助于采用它们并将其纳入标准评价做法[15]。
尽管有这种广泛的热情,但有一批工作提醒说,这种采纳可能为时过早,因为与法学专业人员的有效性和可靠性有关的许多问题已经记录在案[111、91、92、42、27、57、9、34]。

blocks.en:
Human evaluation, despite its drawbacks in practice [ 20 , 112 ] , is supported by an established body of literature that articulates norms to ground evaluations in their broader context [ 84 , 25 ] . In contrast, LLJs lower the barrier to evaluation to an unprecedented degree. This offers scalability and ease of use, but may encourage decontextualized or under-specified evaluation setups [ 15 , 23 , 34 ] . Crockett and Messeri [21] argue that many evaluations have become DEAD —that is, decontextualized, engineered, anonymized, and disembodied —a characterization that maps closely onto current uses of LLJs. Decontextualized use of LLJs refers to their deployment with little specification of the intended audience for the evaluation or the domain of application. For instance, work leveraging LLJs for text summarization [ 60 , 29 , 94 ] rarely clarifies what types of summaries are being evaluated or for which real-world applications. Evaluations are also highly engineered : in safety assessment, complex sociotechnical notions of harm are often reduced to simplified judgments, such as binary preferences over whether content is harmful or not [ 14 ] . Finally, many evaluation setups remain anonymized . A striking example is data labeling, where annotator demographics are often omitted, or, in the case of LLJs, where the positionality of the model is left unspecified [ 13 ] , despite extensive evidence that such factors meaningfully shape the construction of datasets and evaluation outcomes [ 86 ] * * * As Crockett and Messeri [21] ’s work was initially targeted towards cognitive scientist, embodied intelligence is outside the scope of this paper. .
As a result, LLJs run the risk of exacerbating known problems in evaluation by reducing the “good friction” that is rigorous operationalization and systematic validation.
While researchers have proposed methods to test these models [ 58 , 108 ] , improve their reliability [ 89 , 23 ] , or automatically validate their use [ 31 , 34 ] , existing solutions mostly focus on targeted technical fixes. In this paper, we examine how practitioners and researchers evaluation practices can be improved.

blocks.en:
Documentation is recognized as an important mechanism for improving both research and development practices. Bender and Friedman [10] argue that documenting design decisions can advance both scientific and ethical practice by encouraging critical reflection on how these decisions shape system behavior, thereby supporting generalizability and reproducibility. Documentation can also promote more responsible AI development by disclosing potential limitations and shortcomings and supporting external auditing [ 19 ] . In parallel, research on reproducibility has shown that thorough documentation can facilitate system reuse while reducing the risk of misinterpreting or overstating system capabilities [ 66 ] .
Building on these insights, we introduce LLJ Cards , a framework for improving the design and validation of LLJ-based evaluations while increasing transparency.
Our framework draws on established practices from measurement theory [ 1 , 46 , 107 ] , the computational social science [ 99 , 84 ] , natural language generation evaluation (NLG) [ 112 , 40 , 2 ] and responsible AI research [ 90 , 12 ] .
This framework supports practitioners in designing and validating LLMs as judges through a structured set of guiding questions that promote more rigorous, reproducible, and transparent evaluation practices. Our cards make explicit the design choices underlying an evaluation and situate its results within the broader evaluation context, enabling clearer reporting of system capabilities, facilitating reuse, and helping clarify the extent to which findings may generalize beyond the original evaluation setting. By prompting practitioners to systematically reflect on their design choices, LLJ Cards provides a structured basis for transparent reporting and validation.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
LLMs as Judges. In recent years, LLJs have emerged as a preferred evaluation method across a wide range of tasks and applications [ 7 , 60 , 51 , 102 , 43 , 29 , 53 , 15 ] .
While LLJs offer an important opportunity to enable scalable evaluation,
a growing body of work has shown potential limitations in their use, highlighting issues of reliability [ 111 , 91 , 57 , 9 ] , validity [ 92 , 42 , 27 , 34 ] , and robustness [ 83 ] , as well as the extent to which LLJ-based evaluation processes may embed or amplify biases [ 109 , 103 , 74 , 61 , 55 , 52 , 17 , 54 ] . [ 15 ] review the literature on the topic and link some of these pitfalls to existing evaluation practices in the field.
Furthermore, prior work addressing concerns about LLJs validity and reliability has proposed benchmarks and automated test suites to evaluate their performance [ 23 , 26 , 31 ] . For instance, [ 23 ] identify common pitfalls in the use of LLJs and outline experimental protocols to mitigate them. [ 26 ] introduce an automated evaluation suite for assessing LLJ quality, while [ 31 ] propose a training-free framework that generates checklists to improve LLJ systems in multilingual settings.
In contrast to this body of work focused on technical interventions, LLJ Cards aim to improve practitioners’ evaluation practices.

虽然法学法官为能够进行可扩展评价提供了一个重要机会,
越来越多的工作显示出其使用方面的潜在局限性,突出了可靠性[111、91、57、9]、有效性[92、42、27、34]和稳健性[83]的问题,以及基于法学硕士的评价程序可能嵌入或扩大偏见的程度[109、103、74、61、55、52、17、54]。
此外,以前为解决对有限责任法官的有效性和可靠性的关切而开展的工作提出了评估其业绩的基准和自动测试套件[23、26、31]。 例如,[23] 找出使用有限责任会计师的共同陷阱,并概述减轻这些陷阱的实验协议。 [26] 引入一套自动评价套件,用于评估法学硕士的质量,同时[31] 提出一个无培训框架,生成核对表,以改进多种语言环境中法学硕士系统。
与这一系列侧重于技术干预的工作相反,法学专业人员卡的目的是改进从业人员的评价做法。

blocks.en: Measurement Theory. Originating in the quantitative social sciences, measurement theory has been shaped by longstanding efforts to develop rigorous approaches for operationalizing and validating theoretical, often abstract, constructs (e.g., democracy). Adcock and Collier [1] introduce a four-level framework to depict the relationship between concepts and observations: (1) the background concept, which includes all possible definitions of the concept to be measured; (2) the systematized concept, which is a specific formulation of that concept along with its definition; (3) the indicators, which are the measures used to score cases; and (4) the scores, which are the resulting outcomes of the measurement process. They define measurement as encompassing everything required to move from a systematized concept to observed scores [ 1 ] : within this framework, a measurement is valid when the scores produced by an indicator—in our case an LLM as judge—can be meaningfully interpreted in relation to the systematized concept it is intended to assess. A body of work has looked at how this framework could be adapted for NLG evaluation [ 112 , 46 , 101 ] , we build on top of this literature and structure our LLJ Cards around it * * * Consequently, we do not include considerations related to the background concept. . See Figure 1 for an illustration.
blocks.zh: 测量理论. 计量理论起源于定量社会科学,是长期努力制定严格的方法来操作和验证理论,往往是抽象的构造(如民主)而形成的. Adcock and Collier [1] 引入了一个四级框架来描述概念与观察之间的关系: (1)背景概念,包括所有可能用来测量的概念的定义; (2) 系统化的概念,是这一概念及其定义的具体表述; (3) 指标,是用来评分案例的衡量标准; (4) 分数,是测量过程的结果. 它们将衡量定义为包括从系统化概念向观察分数[1]移动所需的一切:在这一框架内,当一项指标所产生的分数——就我们而言是作为判断的衡量标准——能够结合它打算评估的系统化概念得到有意义的解释时,衡量是有效的。 已经研究了如何调整这一框架,以用于NLG的评价[112, 46, 101],我们在此文献的基础上再接再厉,并围绕它构建我们的LLJ卡* 因此,我们不包括与背景概念有关的考虑。 插图1。

Documenting Practices. Responsible AI research has long emphasized the importance of documenting technical artifacts such as datasets, models, and systems [ 10 , 72 , 4 , 65 , 30 , 11 , 62 , 113 ] . Among the most widely adopted proposals, Gebru et al. [30] introduce Datasheets for Datasets , a structured set of guiding questions designed to document dataset creations, while Mitchell et al. [72] extend this idea to model reporting through Model Cards . These approaches aim to standardize documentation practices, support practitioners in recording key decisions about their artifacts, and improve transparency in the field. Similarly, Liu et al. [62] focus on documenting practitioners’ design choices in system development and on guiding them in collecting validity evidence for benchmark-based measurement. While Zhu et al. [113] propose a checklist to guide practionners through agentic benchmarks assessment for validity.
We introduce LLJ Cards to guide LLJ users toward a more valid and reliable use of LLJs through a set of guiding questions grounded in evaluation best practices.

blocks.en: 3 Designing the LLJ Cards
blocks.zh: 3 设计LLJ卡

blocks.en:
We introduce LLJ Cards , a framework to support ML researchers and practitioners—hereafter referred to as “LLJ users”—in developing valid and reliable measurement tools. LLJ Cards guide users through key considerations when designing and using LLJs, helping them avoid common pitfalls, adopt best practices, and promote more standardized and reproducible evaluation practices.
To ensure that our framework is broadly applicable, we ground our approach in representative use cases for each of each of the three functionalities described by Li et al. [56] , following [ 16 ] : text summarization, safety alignment, and data labeling.
blocks.zh:
我们引进了LLJ卡,这是一个支持ML研究人员和从业人员(以下称为 " LLJ用户 " )开发有效和可靠的计量工具的框架。 法学长 卡片指导用户在设计和使用有限责任法官时考虑关键因素,帮助他们避免常见的陷阱,采用最佳做法,并促进更标准化和可复制的评价做法。
为了确保我们的框架得到广泛适用,我们采用具有代表性的个案方法处理李等人所述三个功能中的每一个功能。 [56],后[16]:文本汇总,安全校正,以及数据标签.

blocks.en:
To design our LLJ Cards framework, we first identified the key
desiderata of a successful evaluation [ 47 , 73 , 88 , 21 , 69 , 70 , 71 , 1 , 79 ] , before examining literature in each of the selected use cases.
For each use case, we review the literature to characterize what constitutes a “good evaluation,” document known limitations and failure modes, and extract best practices transferable to our setting.
We considered both automated and human-led evaluation methods, as well as relevant work from adjacent disciplines (e.g., information theory [ 105 , 38 , 39 ] , computational social science [ 80 , 22 , 50 ] , cybersecurity [ 77 , 104 , 81 , 45 ] ), to complement our findings.
We then reviewed LLJ applications for each use case to understand how they are employed in practice [ 60 , 29 , 18 , 94 , 102 , 63 , 97 , 53 , 7 , 95 , 44 ] , alongside literature on their biases and limitations to identify current shortcomings [ 15 , 57 , 98 ] .
Based on this review, we translated the best practices and recommendations identified in the literature into the LLJ setting by designing a coherent workflow aligned with current LLJ practices.
blocks.zh:
为了设计我们的LLJ卡框架,我们首先确定了关键
成功评价[47、73、88、21、69、70、71、1、79],然后审查每一选定使用案例的文献。
对于每种用途,我们审查文献,以说明什么是“良好评价”,记录已知的局限性和失败模式,并摘录可转让给我们的最佳做法。
我们认为,自动化和人主导的评价方法以及相邻学科的相关工作(例如信息理论[105、38、39]、计算社会科学[80、22、50]、网络安全[77、104、81、45])是对我们调查结果的补充。
然后,我们审查了每个使用案例的LLJ申请,以便了解这些申请在实践中是如何使用的[60、29、18、94、102、63、97、53、7、95、44],同时审查关于这些申请的偏见和局限性的文献,以查明目前的缺点[15、57、98]。
根据这次审查,我们设计了一个与目前法学界做法一致的工作流程,将文献中确定的最佳做法和建议转化为法学界设置。

blocks.en:
Our literature review led us to the following LLJ workflow: LLJ users first identify the cases they wish to evaluate and define the type of evaluation to conduct. They then select appropriate evaluation criteria and set up their LLJ pipeline. Next, they typically perform a form of LLJ tuning—such as model selection, prompt engineering, or hyperparameter tuning—before selecting their final pipeline. Finally, they use the LLJ pipeline to score all cases and report the results along with an overall assessment of the LLJ validity, typically by measuring its correlation with a reference metric of their choice.
However, this final validation step captures only one aspect of validity: whether the LLJ produces scores that align with a chosen reference metric. According to Messick [71] , a valid evaluation should also consider the broader consequences of using the LLJ and its resulting scores.
blocks.zh:
我们的文献审查使我们得出了以下法学法学工作流程: LLJ用户首先确定他们希望评价和界定评价类型的情况。 他们然后选择适当的评价标准,并设置其LLJ管道. 其次,它们通常在选择最后输油管之前进行某种形式的LLJ调试——如模型选择、即时工程或超参数调试。 最后,他们利用法学研究管道对所有案例进行评分,并报告结果和对法学研究有效性的总体评估,通常通过衡量其与自己选择的参考衡量标准的相关性。
然而,这个最后的验证步骤只捕捉到有效性的一个方面: LLJ是否产生与所选的参考度量衡一致的分数. 根据Messick [71],有效的评价也应考虑使用LLJ及其产生的分数的更广泛的后果.

blocks.en: Following this workflow, we introduce five cards to document and facilitate the use and understanding of LLJs: Context ( 4.1 ), Evaluation Criteria ( 4.2 ), LLJ Prototyping ( 4.5 ), LLJ Pipeline ( 4.3 ), and LLJ Evaluation ( 4.4 ).

blocks.en: 4 LLJ Cards: Best Practices for the Use of LLMs as Judges
blocks.zh: 4个LLJ 纸牌 : 利用法学硕士作为法官的最佳做法

blocks.en: This framework is designed to help LLJ users throughout the process of using an LLJ. In this section, we first introduce a card before providing a more detailed description of recommended practices for LLJ users, along with examples illustrating their importance.

blocks.en: 4.1 Context
blocks.zh: 4.1 背景情况

blocks.en: In the Context Card , LLJ users are asked to provide contextual information across four axes: the application, the task, the cases, and the evaluation stakeholders.
blocks.zh: 在背景卡中,LLJ用户被要求提供涉及四个轴心的背景资料:应用程序、任务、案例和评价利益攸关方。

blocks.en: Application. LLJ users should describe the real-world context of the application—or, when none is explicitly defined, outline plausible deployment scenarios ( Q. 4 )—and discuss the known risks associated with that environment ( Q. 4 ). For example, deploying an automated text summarization system in a healthcare setting—where summaries may inform decision-making—entails far higher stakes than using a similar system to generate book reviews on an online forum. Consequently, the criteria and priorities guiding the evaluation will differ accordingly.
blocks.zh: 申请. LLJ用户应当描述应用程序的现实背景——或者,在没有明确界定的情况下,概述合理的部署情况(问题4)——并讨论与这种环境有关的已知风险(问题4)。 例如,在保健环境中部署自动文本汇总系统(摘要可能为决策提供依据)比使用类似系统在在线论坛上编写书籍评论要重要得多。 因此,指导评价的标准和优先事项将相应不同。

blocks.en:
Task. LLJ user should provide contextual information about the task in which the LLJ is being leveraged ( Q. 4 ), its known limitations ( Q. 4 ) and potential biases ( Q. 4 ).
For example, safety classifiers and other automated content moderation tools are known to exhibit biases against marginalized groups, including Black [ 35 ] and queer [ 24 ] online communities.
blocks.zh:
任务 LLJ用户应提供有关LLJ被利用的任务(问题4)、其已知的局限性(问题4)和潜在偏见(问题4)的背景资料。
例如,据了解,安全分类员和其他自动内容节制工具对边缘化群体,包括黑人[35]和同性恋[24]在线社区,表现出偏见。

blocks.en:
Cases. LLJ users should provide contextual information about the cases, since building an LLJ pipeline to evaluate them requires clearly defining what they are (e.g., generated automated summaries to evaluate, an existing dataset for labeling, etc.) ( Q. 4 ). This includes how the data was collected, its domain, its scope and limitations, the values and perspectives encoded in it, and whether it is being reused for a purpose different from the one it was originally intended for.
For example, user review ratings are often used as targets in sentiment-based opinion summarization to extract key product aspects [ 96 ] . However, because reviews often contain mixed opinions [ 41 ] , ratings can miss such nuance, introducing noise and undermining evaluation when treated as ground truth [ 3 ] .
blocks.zh:
办案 LLJ用户应提供有关案件的背景信息,因为要建立LLJ管道来评价案件,就必须明确界定案件内容(如生成用于评价的自动摘要、用于标签的现有数据集等)。 (问题4). 这包括数据是如何收集的、其领域、范围和局限性、其中编码的值和视角,以及其是否被重新利用,以达到与原先目的不同的目的。
例如,用户审查评级在基于情绪的意见汇总中常被用作目标,以提取关键产品方面[96]. 然而,由于审查中往往含有不同意见[41],因此,如果将评分视为地面真相,那么评分可能会错失这种细微差别,引起噪音,破坏评价。

blocks.en:
Stakeholders. LLJ users should provide additional context about the evaluation process, including whether the LLJ is being used in a production setting or for an academic study, who is funding its use, and when the evaluation is taking place ( Q. 4 ). We also suggest discussing the intended audience, as it will influence the evaluation design ( Q. 4 ).
Finally, we ask LLJ users to disclose their own background, as well as that of the broader research team ( Q. 4 ). This statement may include a discussion of how the LLJ users’ educational background and training, as well as sociohistorical factors such as nationality, race, gender, class, or other identities, could influence the outcomes of the project [ 86 , 87 , 82 ] . For example, Patton et al. [76] emphasize the need for domain experts when annotating data from marginalized communities, showing strong disagreement between annotators familiar with gang-related activity and those who are not. Similarly, Fleisig et al. [28] demonstrate that annotators’ demographics can influence labels in hate speech detection tasks.
blocks.zh:
利益攸关方。 法学硕士的用户应提供更多关于评价过程的背景,包括:法学硕士是用于生产环境还是用于学术研究,由谁来资助其使用,以及何时进行评价(问题4)。 我们还建议讨论预定对象,因为这将影响评价的设计(问题4)。
最后,我们要求LLJ用户披露自己的背景,以及更广泛的研究团队的背景(问题4). 这一声明可以包括讨论法学工作者的教育背景和培训,以及诸如国籍、种族、性别、阶级或其他身份等社会历史因素如何影响项目的结果[86、87、82]。 例如,巴顿等人. [76] 强调在对边缘化社区的数据进行注释时需要域专家,表明熟悉帮派相关活动的注释者与那些不熟悉的注释者之间存在强烈分歧。 同样, Fleisig等人[28] 证明,在仇恨言论侦测任务中,注释者的人口统计可以影响标签。

blocks.en: The Context Card aims to encourage LLJ users to ground their work within its broader sociotechnical context. Grote [32] defines the evaluation process as riddled with “epistemic and morally normative considerations” as AI systems and other technical artifacts cannot be considered in isolation, but should instead be conceived as tools used for specific purposes with the potential to impact their societal environment [ 32 ] . This perspective aligns with scholars’ call for an adequacy-for-purpose view [ 2 , 75 ] ; that is, the importance of assessing models and other technical artifacts with respect to their success and reliability in a particular instance of use: they should stand with respect to a target, a user, a methodology, circumstances and a purpose [ 75 ] . This view also aligns with Jones and others [48] , who argue that a summary’s usefulness depends on who it is for, what it will be used for, and when it will be used. Here, the technical artifact is seen as a solution in a problem space [ 75 ] that we want to define. We ask for additional background information about the evaluation stakeholders since prior work has shown that such information can meaningfully shape design choices. This reflects the importance of embracing reflexivity [ 86 ] and acknowledging how our background and perspectives inform and constrain project results. We encourage LLJ users to not only think about their own background but also about the values and perspectives encoded in all the technical artifacts (e.g., datasets [ 86 ] or models [ 13 ] ) they are using as measurement inherently involves value judgments at every stage of the process * * * As discussed by Heisenberg [36] : “What we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning” . .
blocks.zh: 《背景卡》旨在鼓励法学工作者在更广泛的社会技术背景下开展工作。 Grote [32] 将评价过程定义为充满“普遍和道德规范的考虑”,因为AI系统和其他技术文物不能孤立地考虑,而应将其视为用于特定目的的工具,有可能影响其社会环境[32]。 这种观点与学者们呼吁以适当方式看待问题[2、75];即评估模型和其他技术文物在具体使用情况下的成功和可靠性的重要性:它们应站在目标、用户、方法、情况和目的[75]。 这种观点也与琼斯等人[48]一致,他们认为总结的有用性取决于它为谁服务,它会用于什么,以及何时使用. 在这里,技术文物被视为我们想要定义的问题空间中的一个解决方案[75]. 我们要求提供更多关于评价利益攸关方的背景资料,因为先前的工作表明,这种信息能够有意义地影响设计选择。 这反映了接受反射[86]的重要性,并承认我们的背景和观点如何通报和制约项目成果。 我们鼓励LLJ用户不仅考虑他们自己的背景,而且考虑所有技术文物(例如数据集[86]或模型[13])中编码的价值观和视角,它们作为衡量方法,在过程的每一阶段都必然涉及价值判断* * * 如海森堡[36]所述: “我们观察到的不是自然本身,而是受到我们质疑方法影响的性质”。

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation Criteria
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价标准

blocks.en: In the Evaluation Criteria Card , LLJ users should document their evaluation goals, including the systematized concept, how it is operationalized, and the limitations of that operationalization.
blocks.zh: 在评价标准卡中,法学工作者的用户应记录其评价目标,包括系统化概念、其操作方式以及这种操作的局限性。

blocks.en:
Systematized Concept. LLJ users should first reflect on the goal of the evaluation by thinking about what they are trying to evaluate and what a perfect scenario would look like ( Q. 4 - 4 ). LLJ users do not necessarily need to redefine the construct they are trying to evaluate; they can rely on existing literature.
For instance, early work by Mani [68] characterizes summary quality along two primary dimensions: informativeness and acceptability and has served as a foundational framework for the development of evaluation metrics, including ROUGE [ 59 ] .
LLJ users should also reflect on the potential ethical considerations associated with the evaluation process, including whether the test is appropriate in the first place [ 69 ] ( Q. 4 ). For example, work in machine psychology often applies psychological assessments developed for humans directly to LLMs and draws conclusions from their responses, rather than first redefining psychological constructs in ways that are appropriate for LLMs [ 64 ] .
blocks.zh:
系统化概念. LLJ用户应该首先思考评价的目标,思考他们正在试图评价什么,一个完美的情景会是什么样子(问题4-4 ) 。 LLJ用户不一定需要重新定义他们试图评价的构造;他们可以依赖现有的文献.
例如,马尼的早期工作[68]将摘要质量分为两个主要方面:信息性和可接受性,并已成为制定评价衡量标准的基础框架,包括ROUGE[59]。
LLJ用户还应当思考与评价过程有关的潜在道德考虑,包括测试是否首先合适[69] (问题4). 例如,机器心理学方面的工作往往将为人类直接开发的心理评估应用于LLMs,并从他们的反应中得出结论,而不是首先以适合LLMs[64]的方式重新定义心理构造.

blocks.en:
Operationalization. Once the systematized concept is clearly defined, LLJ users should specify how it is operationalized, namely through explicit evaluation criteria and their associated definitions ( Q. 4 - 4 ). They should draw on prior work by experts in evaluation to identify and define these criteria ( Q. 4 ), rather than introducing ad hoc definitions. If new criteria and definitions are proposed, LLJ users should explain how they were validated ( Q. 4 ).
Furthermore, it is important to consider the context in which the evaluation criteria were originally defined, and whether this context affects their applicability when reused in a different setting ( Q. 4 ). For instance, defining evaluation criteria for summarization is crucial, as different operationalizations capture different notions of what constitutes a good summary. Intrinsic metrics emphasize coherence and informativeness, often in tension, whereas extrinsic metrics evaluate usefulness in downstream tasks [ 68 ] .
blocks.zh:
业务化. 一旦系统化的概念得到明确定义,法学法学用户就应具体说明其如何运作,即通过明确的评价标准及其相关定义(问题4-4),他们应利用专家在评价中以前的工作,确定和界定这些标准(问题4),而不是采用临时定义。 如果提出了新的标准和定义,法律工作者应解释如何加以验证(问题4)。
此外,还必须考虑到最初界定评价标准的背景,以及这种背景是否影响其在不同的环境下重新使用时的适用性(问题4)。 例如,界定总结的评价标准至关重要,因为不同的可操作性涵盖构成良好总结的不同概念。 内在计量法强调一致性和资料性,往往处于紧张状态,而外在计量法则评价下游任务的有用性[68]。

blocks.en:
Limitations. As the operationalization process provides a proxy for measuring the underlying systematized concept, certain dimensions may not be captured by the chosen criteria. It is therefore important to disclose the potential limitations of the operationalization, as these will affect subsequent interpretations of the system ( Q. 4 ).
For example, collecting harmless preferences has become central to safety alignment research [ 6 ] . While Bai et al. [6] explicitly avoided defining “harmlessness” to encourage diversity, follow-up work shows that preference datasets still tend to reflect Western and majority perspectives [ 49 ] .
Finally, LLJ users should also consider whose values are being used as the standard [ 69 ] and what implications this entails ( Q. 4 ).
blocks.zh:
限制。 由于操作化过程为衡量基本的系统化概念提供了一个代称,某些维度可能无法被选定的标准所捕捉. 因此,必须披露运作可能存在的局限性,因为这些限制将影响随后对系统的解释(问题4)。
例如,收集无害偏好已成为安全调整研究的核心[6]. 时白等. [6] 后续工作明确避免为鼓励多样性而界定“无害”,表明偏好数据集仍然倾向于反映西方和多数人的观点[49]。
最后,法学硕士的使用者还应考虑将哪些价值用作标准[69],以及这会产生什么影响(问题4)。

blocks.en:
The Evaluation Criteria Card aims to support LLJ users through the operationalization process.
Once the context surrounding the use of the LLJ has been identified, a critical step in the evaluation process is to clearly define and document what is being evaluated.
A body of work has shown that the ML and NLP communities have often struggled to clearly define the systematized concept under evaluation and to properly operationalize it [ 12 ] .
As such, we propose a set of guiding questions to help LLJ users better reflect on the goals of their evaluation. This section should be considered independently of the measurement tool chosen by researchers and practitioners. Both the definition of what is being evaluated and how this concept has been characterized in the literature should precede any decision about the indicators. In particular, study design should not be driven by the capabilities of the evaluation tool—in this case, the LLJ—but instead guided by the underlying goal of the evaluation.
blocks.zh:
评价标准 卡片旨在通过操作过程支持LLJ用户.
一旦确定了使用有限责任司法的背景,评价进程中的一个关键步骤是明确界定和记录正在评价的内容。
一组工作表明,劳动和劳工部和NLP社区往往努力明确界定正在评价的系统化概念,并使其适当运作 [12]。
因此,我们提出一套指导性问题,帮助法学工作者更好地思考其评价的目标。 这一部分应独立于研究人员和从业人员选择的衡量工具。 在就指标作出任何决定之前,应先界定正在评估的内容和文献中对这一概念的特征。 特别是,研究设计不应由评价工具的能力所驱动——在此情况下是法学法学硕士——而应以评价的基本目标为指导。

blocks.en: 4.3 LLJ Pipeline
blocks.zh: 4.3 法学硕士 管道

blocks.en: In the LLJ Pipeline Card , LLJ users should document their implementation, including the initial setup, the model(s) used, the final prompt(s), and the scoring function.
blocks.zh: 在LLJ管道卡(英语:LLJ Pipeline Card)中,LLJ的用户应该记录其执行,包括初始设置,所使用的模型,最终的提示,以及评分函数.

blocks.en: Set-Up. LLJ users should report the functionality of the LLJ ( Q. 4 )—whether it is used for data-related tasks, training, or evaluation [ 56 ] —as well as the type of configuration employed ( Q. 4 ). This includes specifying whether they are using an LLJ alone, as part of an ensemble of models, or in combination with a human-in-the-loop evaluation process [ 56 ] . We also ask LLJ users to indicate what is being evaluated ( Q. 4 ) (e.g., automated summaries in English, tweets for hate speech, etc.), along with the evaluation type ( Q. 4 ): pointwise, pairwise, or listwise, etc.—i.e., whether the assessment involves absolute or relative comparisons. For example, pairwise evaluation is particularly popular in safety alignment, when collecting LLM-based preferences to train a model [ 53 , 7 , 95 ] .
blocks.zh: Set-Up. LLJ用户应报告LLJ(Q. 4)的功能——无论是用于与数据有关的任务,培训,还是评价[56]——以及所使用的配置类型(Q. 4). 这包括具体说明他们是否单独使用有限责任会计师,作为模型组合的一部分,或与 " 即时 " 评估过程相结合[56]。 我们还要求法学法学用户说明正在评价什么(问题4)(例如英语自动摘要、仇恨言论的推文等),以及评价类型(问题4):指针、对针或列表等——即评价是否涉及绝对比较或相对比较。 例如,在收集基于LLM的偏好以训练一种模型[53, 7, 95]时,双向评价在安全对齐中特别流行.

blocks.en:
Model. LLJ users should report details of the final model selected for their evaluation ( Q. 4 ), including the model family, version, size, date of access, and any sampling parameters used. They should also briefly justify their choice of model (e.g., state-of-the-art performance in the literature, open-source availability, or privileged access). In addition to documenting the LLJ, users should provide information about whether the model used is proprietary, if an open-source evaluation is provided and if the evaluation code is made publicly available ( Q. 4 ).
LLJ users should also report the costs and resources required for the final evaluation ( Q. 4 ). This may include API expenses for proprietary models or computational requirements for open-source models.
blocks.zh:
型号。 LLJ用户应报告为评价而选择的最后模型的细节(问题4),包括模型家族、版本、大小、访问日期以及所使用的任何抽样参数。 它们还应简要地说明其选择模型的理由(例如,文献中最先进的表现、开放源码的可用性或优先使用)。 除了记录LLJ外,用户还应提供信息,说明所使用的模式是否是专有的,是否提供了开源评价,以及评价代码是否公开(问题4).
LLJ用户还应报告最后评价所需的费用和资源(问题4)。 这可包括专有模型的API费用或开源模型的计算要求.

blocks.en: Prompt. LLJ users should provide examples of all final prompts they are using in their evaluation ( Q. 4 ). Best practices in prompt engineering usually recommend a prompt to have the following components: role, instructions, examples, chain-of-though or other prompt optimization strategy and input and output format [ 110 ] . In the context of LLJs, the literature typically relies on an instruction—although some work has explored the use of personas for LLJ [ 106 ] —followed by an evaluation criterion and its definition (optional). Additional examples for few-shot learning or chain-of-thought can also be integrated, some users also request the LLJ to provide an explanation for the prediction. We refer the readers’ to Li et al. [56] for a more comprehensive account of potential LLJ design configurations. LLJ prompts can also contain reference material; for instance, in text summarization tasks, LLJ users may include a human-written gold summary as a benchmark for what an “ideal” summary should resemble, along with guidance on the expected output format. In all cases, LLJ users are expected to report their final prompt(s) to ensure reproducibility.
blocks.zh: 快点 LLJ用户应举例说明他们在评价中使用的所有最后提示(问题4)。 即时工程的最佳做法通常建议即时具备以下组成部分:角色,指令,实例,虽然的链或其他即时优化策略以及输入和输出格式[110]. 在法学法学家方面,文献通常依赖一种指示——虽然有些工作已经探讨过对法学法学家使用人称法[106]——接着是评价标准及其定义(可选)。 少数镜头学习或思维链的其他例子也可以整合,一些用户还要求LLJ为预测提供解释. 我们请读者参看李等人。 [56]用于更全面地说明潜在的LLJ设计配置. LLJ提示也可以包含参考材料;例如,在文本归纳任务中,LLJ用户可以将人文金文摘要作为“理想”摘要应该相似的基准,同时提供关于预期产出格式的指导。 在所有情况下,LLJ用户都须报告其最后的及时性,以确保可复制。

blocks.en:
Score. After scoring the cases, the LLJ typically produces an output that must be processed, either (1) to extract the final prediction or (2) to further transform the scores to account for LLM reliability issues and hallucinations.
We expect LLJ users to inform these extra steps in ( Q. 4 ) and to justify their post-processing choices ( Q. 4 ).
For example, when leveraging an LLJ for generating pairwise preferences for reinforcement learning with AI feedback, [ 53 ] extract the log probabilities of generating the tokens “1” and “2” and apply a softmax to obtain a preference distribution used as the final score.
blocks.zh:
分数. 在给案例打分后,LLJ通常会产生必须处理的输出,要么(1)提取最终预测,要么(2)进一步转换分数,以说明LLM可靠性问题和幻觉.
我们期望LLJ用户在(问题4)中告知这些额外步骤,并证明其处理后选择的理由(问题4)。
例如,在利用LLJ生成双向偏好,以人工智能反馈进行强化学习时,[53]提取生成符号“1”和“2”的日志概率,并应用软码以获得用作最终分数的偏好分布。

blocks.en:
The LLJ Pipeline Card aims to help LLJ users thoroughly document their final LLJ pipeline. Reproducibility is essential for valid and reliable evaluation, as it ensures that the process can be repeated and produces consistent results and conclusions [ 78 ] . However, in the context of LLJs, this assumption does not hold in practice. Many LLJ approaches rely on proprietary models that may be updated or deprecated without notice [ 60 ] , making exact replication inherently difficult. Even when studies attempt to document their setups, key details are frequently underspecified—for instance, by referring to “off-the-shelf” models [ 7 ] or to “ChatGPT” without specifying exact versions, omitting hyperparameters, or not fully reporting the content of prompts used in evaluation [ 15 ] .
As a result, many LLJ pipelines are only partially reproducible. This card aims to address this under-specification by guiding LLJ users on the minimal information they should report to improve reproducibility and transparency. We structure it based on the conception of an LLJ system proposed by Li et al. [56] .
blocks.zh:
LLJ管道 卡片旨在帮助LLJ用户彻底记录他们最后的LLJ管道. 可复制性对于有效和可靠的评价至关重要,因为它确保了这一过程可以重复,并产生一致的结果和结论[78]。 然而,就法学法学人员而言,这一假设在实践中并不成立。 许多LLJ方法依赖于专利模型,这些模型可能在不事先通知的情况下更新或贬值[60],使确切的复制本身变得困难. 即使在研究试图记录其设置时,关键细节也往往不够明确,例如,提到 " 现成 " 模型[7]或 " ChatGPT " 没有具体说明确切的版本,省略了超参数,或没有充分报告评价中使用的提示的内容[15]。
因此,许多LLJ管道只能部分再生产. 该卡旨在解决这种规格不足的问题,指导法学硕士用户了解他们应报告的最低信息,以提高可复制性和透明度。 我们根据李等人提出的法学法学体系概念来构建这一体系。 [56] (中文(简体) ).

blocks.en: 4.4 LLJ Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4.4 法学法官 评价

blocks.en: In the LLJ Evaluation Card , LLJ users should validate the evaluation outcomes as well as discuss the potential societal consequences of the evaluation.
blocks.zh: 在法学硕士评价卡中,法学硕士的用户应验证评价结果并讨论评价可能产生的社会影响。

blocks.en:
Evaluation. LLJ users should report how they evaluated the scores derived from the LLJ outputs: the metrics, benchmarks, baselines, etc. ( Q. 4 ). Popular methods include correlation with human judgment, or performance on a downstream task when the LLJ scores are being used for training. For example, Lee et al. [53] assess the effectiveness of LLM-generated feedback for safety alignment by training a model on such feedback and then employing human evaluators to measure the resulting model’s win rate and harmlessness level.
When evaluating LLJ scores, we also recommend presenting disaggregated results and statistical analysis if appropriate ( Q. 4 ).
We also ask LLJ users to document any tests conducted to assess validity ( Q. 4 ). In this context, correlations with human judgments and comparisons to baseline metrics are commonly used as evidence of convergent validity when validating a judge [ 15 ] .
LLJ users should also disclose the limitations of their evaluation process ( Q. 4 ), including anything excluded from the overall analysis.
Finally, in some cases where the LLJ is intended for production in a dynamic environment, maintenance considerations should be taken into account ( Q. 4 ): how frequently should the LLJ be re-evaluated?
blocks.zh:
评价。 LLJ用户应该报告他们如何评价从LLJ产出中获得的分数:衡量标准,基准,基线等(问题4). 流行的方法包括与人类判断的相关性,或者在LLJ分数被用于培训时对下游任务的表现. 例如,Lee et al. [53] 通过培训关于这种反馈的模型,然后利用人类评估人员衡量模型的胜利率和无害程度,评估LLM产生的反馈对安全协调的有效性。
在评价法学士评分时,我们也建议酌情提出分类结果和统计分析(问题4)。
我们还要求法学专业协会用户记录为评估有效性而进行的任何测试(问题4)。 在这方面,与人类判断的相关性和与基线衡量尺度的比较通常用于证明法官验证时的趋同有效性[15]。
法学硕士的使用者还应披露其评价过程的局限性(问题4),包括被排除在全面分析之外的任何内容。
最后,在某些情况下,如果有限责任会计师打算在动态环境中生产,则应考虑维护因素(问题4):在多大程度上应当重新评价有限责任会计师?

blocks.en:
Ethical Considerations. LLJ users should reflect on the ethical considerations associated with the evaluation process and its outcomes.
As such, we suggest that they begin by considering the potential consequences of a misleading evaluation ( Q. 4 ), within the intended context of use (§ 4.1 ). Taking inspiration from approaches such as impact statements [ 5 ] , LLJ users should reflect on the benefits, risks, and potential uncertainties associated with the measurement process. This includes examining whether the evaluation process introduces or amplifies sources of invalidity related to bias, fairness, and distributive justice [ 71 ] .
Furthermore, because anticipating unintended side effects of an evaluation is hard, we follow Messick [69] suggestion to approach this question comparatively, by contrasting the evaluation potential impacts with those of plausible alternatives ( Q. 4 ). For example, Chehbouni et al. [15] discuss how the field has progressively moved away from computationally efficient metrics (such as ROUGE [ 59 ] ) toward the use of large LLMs, which come with substantially higher computational costs and, consequently, a potentially significant environmental footprint over time.
Finally, LLJ users are asked to reflect on the potential risks and harms that could arise from using the LLJ scores for action ( Q. 4 ), either for decision-making, or or in subsequent applications.
blocks.zh:
道德考虑。 法学专业人员的使用者应反思与评价过程及其结果有关的道德考虑。
因此,我们建议首先在预定的使用范围内考虑误导性评价的潜在后果(问题4)(第4.1节)。 从影响说明[5] 等方法获得启发,法学法律使用者应反思与衡量过程有关的益处、风险和潜在的不确定性。 这包括审查评价过程是否引入或扩大与偏见、公平和分配公正有关的无效来源[71]。
此外,由于预测评价的意外副作用很困难,我们遵循Messick [69]的建议,即通过将评价的潜在影响与可行的替代品的影响相比较,比较处理这一问题(问题4)。 例如,Chehbouni 等人,他们认为,“我们没有为人类创造机会。 [15] 讨论实地如何逐渐从计算效率的度量衡(如ROUGE[59])转向使用大型有限责任公司,后者的计算成本要高得多,因此随着时间的推移,环境足迹可能很大。
最后,LLJ用户被要求思考使用LLJ得分作为行动(问题4),用于决策,或在随后的应用中可能产生的潜在风险和伤害.

blocks.en:
The LLJ Evaluation card aims to help LLJ users inform the final evaluation of the LLJ pipeline.
This includes checking whether the operationalization is consistent with the final scores, whether the results are meaningful, and whether the claims made align with the scope of the process.
While measurement theory emphasizes that validity and reliability are not intrinsic properties of a test, but rather concern the interpretation of scores within a specific context [ 71 ] , existing work on LLJs has often taken the opposite stance. In particular, LLJs are frequently assumed to be validated by prior studies and therefore directly transferable across tasks and settings, without requiring re-validation in new contexts [ 15 , 34 ] .
As such, we encourage LLJ users to interpret the resulting scores in light of their limitations to avoid overgeneralization [ 69 ] : LLJ users may sometimes draw conclusions that exceed what the results can support, without properly validating that these results are generalizable [ 69 ] . Crockett and Messeri [21] refers to this phenomenon as the illusion of generalizability , where the lack of grounding in a specific context enables cognitive scientists to overextend claims and assume their findings apply universally. This illusion of generalizability is also prevalent in the NLP and ML literature, where it has contributed to the promotion of LLJ approaches presented as enabling universal evaluations, “as one desires [ 29 ] .”
blocks.zh:
LLJ评价卡旨在帮助LLJ用户为LLJ管道的最终评价提供信息.
这包括检查操作是否与最终分数一致,结果是否有意义,以及索赔是否符合程序范围。
虽然衡量理论强调有效性和可靠性不是测试的内在性质,而是涉及在特定背景下的分数解释[71],但关于法学法学士的现有工作往往采取相反的立场. 特别是,常常假定法学专业人员通过先前的研究得到验证,因此可在任务和设置上直接转让,而不需要在新的情况下重新验证[15、34]。
因此,我们鼓励LLJ用户根据其局限性来解释所产生的分数,以避免过度概括[69]: LLJ用户有时可能得出超过结果所能支持的结论,但没有适当验证这些结果是笼统的[69]. Crockett and Messeri [21] 将这种现象称为通俗化的幻觉 . . . NLP和ML文献中也普遍存在这种普遍化的幻想,它有助于推广作为促成普遍评价而提出的法学法学方法,“正如人们所期望的[29]”。

blocks.en: 4.5 LLJ Prototyping
blocks.zh: 4.5 法学硕士 原型制作

blocks.en: In the LLJ Prototyping Card , LLJ users should document the prototyping process, including the study setup, tested data, LLJ design and validation, as well as any refinements made during this stage * * * Note that although the LLJ Prototyping stage occurs earlier in the process, we describe it last, as it relies on concepts introduced in the LLJ Pipeline and LLJ Evaluation cards. We do not expect LLJ users to complete LLJ Pipeline and LLJ Evaluation cards for every configuration tested during the prototyping stage; however, the final LLJ pipeline should be thoroughly documented using these cards. .
blocks.zh: 在LLJ原型卡中,LLJ用户应该记录原型制作过程,包括研究设置,测试数据,LLJ设计和验证,以及这一阶段所做的任何改进** 请注意,虽然LLJ原型制作阶段发生在该过程的早期,但我们最后还是描述了它,因为它依赖于LLJ管道和LLJ评价卡中引入的概念. 我们并不期望LLJ用户为在原型制作阶段测试的每个配置完成LLJ管道和LLJ评价卡;但是,最后的LLJ管道应该使用这些卡进行彻底记录. 。 。 。

blocks.en:
Study Set-Up. Based on the purpose of the evaluation (§ 4.1 ,§ 4.2 ), LLJ users should first define the scope, timeline, expected cost of the LLJ prototyping phase, and determine whether specialized expertise is required [ 84 , 77 ] ( Q. 4 ). For example, the smaller scope of this stage allows LLJ users to incorporate more diverse perspectives into the evaluation design process, such as by consulting the intended audience of the evaluation [ 93 , 67 ] (§ 4.1 ).
When determining the scope and depth of testing, Peake [77] recommend first identifying “low-hanging fruit”: the most likely edge cases and known biases in LLJs that can be readily tested and are expected to yield meaningful insights if addressed.
blocks.zh:
研究Set-Up. 根据评价的目的(§ 4.1,§4.2),LLJ用户应首先界定LLJ原型阶段的范围,时间表,预期成本,并确定是否需要专业知识[84,77] (问题4). 例如,这一阶段的较小范围使法学硕士的使用者能够将更加多样化的视角纳入评价设计过程,例如通过咨询评价的预期受众[93,67](§4.1).
在确定测试的范围和深度时,Peake [77] 建议首先确定“低挂果实”:最有可能发现的边缘案例和已知的有限责任法官偏差,这些案例和偏差可以随时测试,如果得到解决,可望产生有意义的见解。

blocks.en:
Data. LLJ users should construct the prototyping dataset which will serve as a baseline for optimizing the LLJ pipeline and assessing its validity.
To maximize its effectiveness, this dataset should include both a random sample of cases and challenging edge-case examples [ 50 , 67 ] , as this increases the likelihood of uncovering potential weaknesses in the design early on ( Q. 4 - 4 ). For example, difficult cases in data labeling might include data points with high disagreement between annotators, while difficult cases in text summaries can refer to summaries with low compression rates.
blocks.zh:
数据. LLJ用户应构建原型数据集,作为优化LLJ管道和评估其有效性的基线。
为了最大限度地提高其有效性,本数据集应当包括随机抽样案例和具有挑战性的边缘案例实例[50,67],因为这增加了早期设计中发现潜在缺陷的可能性(问题4-4)。 例如,数据标签方面的困难案例可能包括注释者之间有较大分歧的数据点,而文本摘要中的困难案例可以指压缩率低的概要.

blocks.en: Design. LLJ users should document and disclose the different model they used, their prompting strategies and configuration choices across all evaluated variants, in line with prior recommendations on reproducibility and reporting in research [ 9 ] ( Q. 4 ). Furthermore, LLJ users should also disclose, if possible, the results of this preliminary tuning process ( Q. 4 ), to increase transparency about potential biases or reliability issues [ 9 ] .
blocks.zh: 设计. LLJ用户应当按照以往关于研究中可复制性和报告性的建议,记录和披露他们使用的不同模式、他们对所有被评价变体的激励战略和配置选择[9](问题4)。 此外,如果可能,有限责任法学用户还应披露这一初步调整过程的结果(问题4),以提高潜在偏见或可靠性问题的透明度[9]。

blocks.en:
Validation. LLJ users should conduct a range of evaluations targeting different forms of validity and reliability to more comprehensively assess the system ( Q. 4 - 4 ).
A useful way to approach this process is to focus on unacceptable behavior: after having defined the system’s desired outputs (§ 4.2 ), we encourage LLJ users to consider what the model should not do, as this “negative space” is often easier to articulate [ 67 , 93 ] . This perspective can then be used to design targeted tests that explicitly probe for such undesirable behaviors.
blocks.zh:
鉴定. 当地法学工作者应针对不同形式的有效性和可靠性进行一系列评价,以便更全面地评估该系统(问题4-4)。
处理这个过程的有益方法是关注不可接受的行为:在定义了系统的预期产出(§4.2)之后,我们鼓励法学硕士用户考虑这个模型不应该做什么,因为这个“负空间”往往更容易表述[67,93]. 然后,这一视角可用于设计目标明确的测试,明确探索此类不良行为。

blocks.en:
Refinement. LLJ users should, after assessing validity, consider whether any refinement of the LLJ pipeline is required, or in some cases whether it is necessary to even modify the systematized concept ( Q. 4 ).
A key question in this refinement process is when to stop ( Q. 4 ): determining what constitutes “good enough” performance is inherently task-dependent and varies across domains, task complexity, and evaluation goals. In some cases, even moderate or imperfect agreement scores may be acceptable if they are consistent with the state of the art or aligned with the intended use of the system.
blocks.zh:
精进精进. LLJ用户在评估有效性后,应考虑是否需要改进LLJ管道,或在某些情况下是否有必要甚至修改系统化的概念(问题4)。
这一完善过程中的一个关键问题是何时停止(问题4):确定什么是“足够好”的业绩,这本身就取决于任务,并且因领域、任务的复杂性和评价目标而异。 在某些情况下,即使是中度或不完善的协议得分,如果符合技术水平或符合系统的预期用途,也可能是可以接受的。

blocks.en:
The LLJ Prototyping card is intended to support LLJ users in designing the final LLJ pipeline and LLJ evaluation protocol.
A common practice in data labeling, which we propose to adopt for LLJ use, is conducting a pilot study [ 50 , 25 , 100 , 84 ] . Pilot studies are small-scale, initial experiments aimed at developing and refining the annotation process until it is sufficiently robust for full-scale deployment [ 50 ] . During this phase, practitioners iteratively improve annotation guidelines, clarify task definitions, and adjust methodological choices [ 50 ] .
Introducing such a phase is particularly important in the context of LLJs, where evaluations can be costly, whether due to API usage or computational demands. A pilot study enables practitioners to identify and address issues early, before committing substantial resources to a flawed evaluation setup [ 50 ] . During pilot studies, it is common to uncover limitations in the annotation guidelines, which may fail to capture certain phenomena, or be ambiguous or difficult for annotators to interpret [ 50 ] . When such issues arise, it is appropriate to revisit the initial guideline design and iteratively refine and improve it before proceeding to full-scale evaluation [ 8 ] . This idea is closely aligned with practices in red-teaming [ 45 ] , where systems are iteratively stress-tested to identify failures and unintended behaviors under challenging conditions.
These benefits make a strong case for incorporating a pilot-study phase as a standard component of LLJ use. Since pilot studies traditionally involve human participants, we refer to the analogous process in LLJ workflows as the LLJ prototyping stage.
Finally, while LLJ users typically already implement some of these practices—such as testing multiple models, prompt engineering, and stress-testing evaluators through prompt sensitivity or position bias checks [ 56 ] —they often do so informally and without consistent documentation. With this card, we aim to formalize the process and improve transparency, while also reducing workload by concentrating the most intensive testing on a small, targeted subsample of cases.
blocks.zh:
法学法官 原型卡旨在支持LLJ用户设计最终的LLJ管道和LLJ评价协议.
在数据标签方面我们建议采用的一种常见做法是进行试点研究[50、25、100、84]。 试点研究是小规模的初步实验,旨在发展和完善注释过程,直至其足够坚固,可以全面部署[50]. 在这一阶段,从业人员反复改进说明准则,澄清任务定义,并调整方法选择[50]。
引入这样一个阶段对于当地法律工作者来说尤其重要,因为无论是由于API的使用还是计算需求,评价费用都可能很高。 试点研究使从业人员能够及早发现和解决问题,然后将大量资源投入有缺陷的评价机构[50]。 在试点研究期间,通常发现注释准则中的局限性,这些局限性可能无法捕捉到某些现象,或者对注释者解释[50]有模棱两可或困难. 在出现这些问题时,在着手进行全面评价之前,应重新审视初步准则设计并反复加以完善和改进[8]。 这个想法与红队的做法紧密结合[45],其中系统进行反复压力测试,以查明在挑战性条件下的失败和意外行为.
这些好处有力地证明,应该将试点学习阶段作为法学法学应用的标准组成部分。 由于试点研究传统上涉及人类参与者,我们把法学研究工作流程中的类似过程称为法学研究原型阶段。
最后,虽然法学硕士的使用者通常已经实施了其中一些做法——例如通过及时的敏感性或位置偏差检查测试多种模型、即时工程和压力测试评估员[56]——但他们经常非正式地这样做,没有一致的文件。 有了这张卡,我们的目标是使这一进程正规化,提高透明度,同时把最密集的测试集中在一个小规模的、有针对性的子样本中,从而减少工作量。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We have introduced a practical tool designed to support the valid and reliable use of LLJs in evaluation settings. Our methodological framework, LLJ Cards , aims to improve evaluation practices while enhancing transparency and reproducibility in the field.
While we hope our framework can be applied to any LLJ implementation, it was primarily developed and illustrated through three applications: text summarization, safety alignment, and data labeling. Although these settings differ substantially in how LLJs are used and correspond to distinct communities of practice, they do not cover the full range of possible LLJ applications.
Our framework is intended to be flexible, however we caution LLJ users about potential limitations in its generalizability across settings.
We believe there is strong promise in scalable automated evaluation when it is done rigorously—for instance, by enabling more realistic, interactive, and long-horizon evaluation pipelines that better reflect real-world usage. However, realizing this potential requires principled and careful use. We hope that our framework contributes to supporting such practice and encourages more responsible deployment of LLJ-based evaluation.
blocks.zh:
我们采用了一种实用工具,旨在支持在评价环境中有效和可靠地使用法学专业人员。 我们的方法框架LLJ卡旨在改进评价做法,同时提高外地的透明度和可复制性。
虽然我们希望我们的框架能够适用于任何有限责任司法的实施,但它主要是通过三个应用程序来制定和说明的:文本汇总、安全调整和数据标签。 虽然这些设置在如何使用有限责任律师和如何与不同的实践群体相对应方面大不相同,但它们并不涵盖所有可能的有限责任律师应用。
我们的框架旨在具有灵活性,但我们要提醒法学硕士的使用者注意其在不同环境中的可概括性可能存在的限制。
我们认为,在严格进行可扩展的自动化评价时,有很强的希望——例如,通过建立更现实、互动和长远的评价管道,更好地反映现实世界的使用情况。 然而,要发挥这一潜力,就必须有原则地认真加以利用。 我们希望,我们的框架有助于支持这种做法,并鼓励更负责任地部署以法学法官为基础的评价。
